heroAlt: Sankey-style deployment matrix mapping $106M in Portland housing funds across eight legally distinct sources, with uncommitted balances in saturated color flowing to recommended program allocations and KPI alignments, dated April 9, 2026.
leads: $106 million in Portland housing funds sat uncommitted with no architecture connecting them to validated interventions — while the shelter system exited 17 percent of people to permanent housing against its own 41 percent goal, and more than 18,000 people went unhoused.

No commission preceded the work. The engagement was a deliberate live test of the Sarif methodology: whether one analyst with an AI-augmented production stack could produce civic intelligence at the standard a council floor demands, delivered cold to the officials who would have to act on it.

Council passed the Keep Portland Housed ordinance days later, committing approximately $56 million — close to the figure the matrix had marked as deployable. We claim the sequence and the analysis, not the causation: two sitting councilors and the executive director of a regional housing coalition responded directly, and the suite was revised twice inside the live budget window to keep pace with implementation.
highlights: Ten-chapter strategic playbook grounded in a ten-city global evidence corpus — including Houston, Helsinki, Glasgow, Bakersfield and Vienna
$106M deployment matrix mapping eight legally distinct funds, committed versus deployable, dollar by dollar
Five-document council suite delivered cold to sitting officials, published via The Living Stack — all five open below
Execution-gap catch: $5.6M committed by council, $0 budgeted by the executing agency twelve days later
Every figure cited to a decision-package ID or verbatim budget quote; silence documented as 'budget does not state'
Direct response from two sitting councilors and the executive director of a regional housing coalition
Created, refined and delivered in ten working days — then re-cut twice inside the live 60-day budget window as council acted.
